title: FILING WINDOW OPENS
full_story:
Anyone planning to run for a local school board seat in Clay County will be able to file their nominating petitions starting this week.

Clay County Clerk Amy Britton has released key dates for the April 6th, Consolidated Election.  Candidates running for school district board seats can file their petitions at the County Clerk’s office from Monday, through Friday, between 8 am and 4 pm.  The filing window will also be open on Monday, November 23rd, from 8 am to 5 pm.

Britton notes that all other petition and caucus information will be handled directly by and filed with each respective local entity.

Along with school district board members, voters in the April Consolidated Election will also decide races for municipal mayors or presidents, clerks, and commissioners or trustees.  Other offices on the ballot include park district commissioners or trustees, regional board of school trustees, community college district trustees, and fire protection district trustees.

Anyone with questions about the upcoming filing process can contact the Clay County Clerk’s office at 618-665-3626.

title: TENTATIVE MULTIPLIER ANNOUNCED
full_story:
Clay County has been issued a tentative property assessment equalization factor of 1.0000, according to David Harris, director of the Illinois Department of Revenue (IDOR).

The property assessment equalization factor, often called the “multiplier,” is the method used to achieve uniform property assessments among counties, as required by law.  This equalization is particularly important because some of the state’s 6,600 local taxing districts overlap into two or more counties (e.g., school districts, junior college districts, fire protection districts).  If there was no equalization among counties, substantial inequities among taxpayers with comparable properties would result.

State law requires property in Illinois to be assessed at one-third (1/3) of its market value.  Farm property is assessed differently with farm homesites and dwellings subject to regular assessing and equalization procedures.  Farmland and farm buildings are assessed according to standards based on productivity.

The equalization factor is determined annually for each county by comparing the sales price of individual properties sold over the past three years to the assessed value placed on those properties by the county supervisor of assessments/ county assessor.

If the three-year average level of assessment is one-third of market value, the equalization factor will be one (1.0000).  If the average level of assessment is greater than one-third of market value, the equalization factor will be less than one (1.0000).  And if the average level of assessment is less than one-third of market value, the equalization factor will be greater than one (1.0000).

Assessments in Clay County are at 33.33% of market value, based on sales of properties in 2023, 2024, and 2025.

The equalization factor currently being assigned is for taxes, 2026 payable in 2027.

The tentative factor is subject to change (1) if the County Board of Review takes actions which significantly affect the county assessments, or (2) if local officials or others can present data showing that IDOR’s estimates of the average level of assessments in the county should be adjusted.  A public hearing on the tentative multiplier will be held between 20 and 30 days after the tentative factor is published in a newspaper of general circulation within the county.

A change in the equalization factor does not mean total property tax bills will increase or decrease.  Tax bills are determined by local taxing bodies when they request money each year to provide services to local citizens.  If the amount requested by local taxing districts is not greater than the amount received in the previous year, then total property taxes will not increase even if assessments may have increased.

The assessed value of an individual property determines what portion of the tax burden a specific taxpayer will assume.  That individual’s portion of tax responsibility is not changed by the multiplier.

title: BLACK DIAMOND ALL CONFERENCE
full_story:
The Black Diamond Conference has named their All-Conference selections for Football.

Flora’s Kormick Massie was named the offensive Captain, with Quarter Back, Thane Warren, Kehlin Crawford, Brennan O’Donnell, and Kormick Massie making the First Team Offense.  Crawford, Massie and O’Donnell were unanimous selections.

Making First Team Defense were Wesley Moore, Andrew Wilson, and Gage Dugan.  Gage Dugan was a unanimous selection.  Making the Second Team Offense was Zane McKinney and Caleb Shehorn and Second Team Defense was Memphis Moore.

Honorable Mention from Flora were Jerron Lewis and Carson Smith, Special Teams with a unanimous selection was Kicker Mateus Tricerri and Connor Brooks got a special mention.

title: PRE-FILING NOTICE
full_story:
Notice is hereby given that the office of the City Clerk of the City of Flora will be open from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm today, through Friday, and open until 5:00 pm on Monday, November 23rd, for the purpose of accepting candidate petitions for the 2027 Consolidated Election to be held on April 6th, for the following offices: Mayor, Commissioner of Accounts and Finances, Commissioner of Public Health and Safety, Commissioner of Public Property, and Commissioner of Streets and Public Improvements.

Petitions should be filed at Flora City Hall, 131 E. Second Street.

A lottery will be held for all simultaneous filings that are filed at 8:00 am this morning or received in today’s mail.  Petitions filed within the last hour of the filing deadline (4:00 pm to 5:00 pm on Monday, November 23rd) shall be deemed filed simultaneously and are included in the lottery drawing to determine the final ballot position.  Should a simultaneous lottery be necessary, it will be scheduled for Wednesday, December 2nd, at 9:15 am in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

The complete Candidate’s Guide is available on the State Board of Elections website at (www.elections.il.gov).

title: SECOND PROPERTY TAX PAYMENT DUE
full_story:
The second installment of the 2025 payable 2026 Real Estate Tax Bill is due this Friday.  If you have questions about your tax bill, please feel free to call the Treasurer’s office.  If you cannot get through, please leave a message, and they will return your call as soon as possible.  Phone 618-665-3727.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.

At the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money order.  Bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00 am to 4:00 pm Monday through Friday but closed on national holidays.

Online by credit/debit card: Go to www.govpaynow.com PLC #a00082.

Or by drop box at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

title: COOKIE WALK & BASKET RAFFLE
full_story:
The St. Stephen Church, in Flora, will be having their annual Christmas Cookie Walk & Basket Raffle on Saturday, December 5th, from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm.

There will be homemade cookies and candy, and a raffle of a large assortment of gift baskets.  You can select your own cookies and candy.  A portion of the proceeds from the sale of cookies and candy will be donated to the Clay County Ministerial Alliance Food Pantry.  A portion of the proceeds from the basket raffle will be donated to Guadalupe Project.

The Christmas Cookie Walk & Basket Raffle is on Saturday, December 5th, from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm.

title: LAKE SHELBYVILLE CLOSURES
full_story:
The US Army Corps of Engineers, St. Louis District, will temporarily close several recreation areas at Lake Shelbyville from 2 pm on Thursday, through 7 pm on Sunday, to accommodate the 36th annual Lake Shelbyville Deer Hunt for People with Disabilities.

The hunt, conducted in partnership with Wolf Creek State Park, will take place this weekend during the first firearm deer season.

As a safety precaution, the following locations will be closed to all vehicle and pedestrian traffic; Lone Point and Lithia Springs campgrounds, Wilborn Creek Recreation Area, Whitley Creek Recreation Area, Coon Creek Recreation Area, and Opossum Creek Recreation Area.

The closures also include boat ramps within the Wilborn Creek, Whitley Creek, Coon Creek and Opossum Creek recreation areas.

Boat ramps at Dam West, Lone Point, Lithia Springs, Forrest W, Bo Woods, Wolf Creek State Park and Eagle Creek State Park will remain open, along with all secondary ramps.  The campground closures at Lone Point and Lithia Springs will not affect access to their boat ramps.

For more information, contact Lake Shelbyville Natural Resources Specialist Taylor Finks at 217-774-3951, ext. 7028.

title: ISP INCREASING PATROLS
full_story:
The Illinois State Police is increasing patrols and ramping up enforcement efforts in advance of the holiday season.  Earlier this month, the ISP began focusing daily resources on I-57 near Mt. Vernon as part of a construction work zone safety initiative.  During the first week in November, ISP issued more than 650 citations and warnings to drivers, completed more than 80 Motor Carrier Safety Inspections, and placed 17 commercial vehicles traveling through these zones Out of Service.

“To help ensure those traveling through the construction zones and those working in it are safe, ISP is increasing collaboration among numerous ISP work units, including Troop 10 Patrol, the Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Bureau, and Special Operations Group, to get drivers to slow down, follow others at a safe distance, move over, and stop driving when distracted – some of the leading causes of crashes,” said ISP Director Brendan F. Kelly.

This high saturation and visibility approach is aimed at deterring speeding and distracted driving in the area to prevent crashes.  In addition to working with ISP to increase patrols, amplify awareness of the project, and address safety in the work zone, the Illinois Department of Transportation has maintained two lanes in each direction during peak or daytime hours, scheduled some of the more impactful work during off-peak hours, reduced speed limits, and added additional lane markings to help guide traffic.

“In any work zone, the people working behind the cones and barricades want to get home safely to their families and loved ones,” said Illinois Transportation Secretary Gia Biagi.  “We appreciate the partnership with Illinois State Police to help build driver awareness and reinforce safer habits when you are behind the wheel in one of our largest, most active work zones anywhere in the state.  Slowing down, following the signs, and avoiding all distractions can save lives – including your own.”

Last year, 50% of crashes ISP handled in Jefferson County occurred in a work zone.  Construction in the two zones on I-57 near Mt. Vernon will continue until June and October 2027.

With this and many other construction projects throughout the state, drivers should allow plenty of time for travel, reduce speed, avoid tailgating, and pay attention to the road.  Speeding, distracted driving, following too closely, and driving while impaired in work zones are serious offenses, which can result in tragic consequences.

The minimum fine for a first offense of speeding in a work zone is $250.  A second offense results in a suspended driver’s license for 90 days and a $750 fine.  If the violation results in injury to another person, the violator’s driver’s license will be suspended for a mandatory period of anywhere between six months and two years.

When approaching a work zone or vehicle with its emergency lights activated, motorists are reminded that the Move Over Law requires them to slow down and move over.  A person who violates the Move Over Law faces a fine of no less than $250 and no more than $10,000 for a first offense.  If the violation results in injury to another person, the violator’s driver’s license will be revoked.  Additional information about ISP related crashes can be found on the ISP Move Over Crash Map.
